GDP only grows three ways... more people, more debt or more productivity. 

More people is gone. Demographics were set in stone 30 years ago and nobody can change them. The workforce is shrinking and ageing, so the growth that used to come from simply adding workers has been fading for two decades.

For the last 15 years the gap left by people has been filled with borrowing, more and more of it, until we're now borrowing to pay the interest on the borrowing. That's the debasement everyone feels but cant name. And that lever is spent too.

Which leaves the third one. Productivity. But here's the problem... productivity has always meant people producing more, and we are running out of people. The only way to get a step change in output with fewer workers is machines.

AI and robotics are not a nice to have. They are the one lever still available, and they are the only thing that can get us out of this mess and outgrow the debt rather than inflate it away.

So yes, people are worried about the robots taking their jobs. The alternative is a system with no way out.

What does change is who the value flows to. It goes to whoever owns the networks...

So if the robots are coming for our jobs, then we had bloody well better own the robots.
